Replaces #1580. The commits are unchanged. This PR uses a personal fork to allow maintainer edits.

## Problem

A large client-rendered Foldkit application cannot activate an unseen route implementation after boot through the public runtime API. Loading a module in a Command does not install its synchronous update, view and Subscriptions. Restarting the Runtime loses the required lifecycle. This is an implementation contribution to #1559, not a claim that downstream performance budgets are already met.

## Decision

Add an optional runtime-owned `lazyComposition` channel to `Runtime.makeApplication` and `Runtime.makeElement`. Requested and accepted identities remain serializable Model data. The root reducer owns lifecycle acceptance; immutable implementation snapshots remain outside the Model. Successful code stays available for replay and return navigation. Root services, ManagedResources and application-wide Subscriptions retain their runtime lifetime; route Subscriptions follow complete build/key/request identity.

Restored accepted identity loads before first render. Import failures become identity-bearing Messages, retries need a new request identity, and failed resource provision crashes rather than publishing false readiness. Missing accepted implementations fail explicitly. Existing static configurations remain unchanged.

Scope: client rendering only. Hydration rejects this configuration; SSR/SSG resolves statically. This does not add a router, asset retention, modulepreload scheduler or automatic deployment swapping. The maintainer noted on #1559 that adoption may wait until v1; this PR is offered for review, not downstream adoption without a supported release.

## Verification

- Foldkit package and Vite plugin builds pass.
- Foldkit typecheck passes, including six negative undeclared-service cases and declared-Layer controls.
- Lazy lifecycle and inference suites: 15 tests pass across two files.
- Framework/application lint passes.
- Routing example typecheck passes after building its exported UI prerequisite.
- Built routing Chromium suite: four tests pass, one worker, zero retries.
- Real Vite manifest and emitted module graph prove Reports is absent from the initial static closure and dynamically loaded after boot, with one Foldkit and one Effect package root.
- Browser proof preserves the shell node, value and focus across delayed import; re-entry retains counter state without a second Reports request.
- Additional managed Chromium visual smoke: Reports loads, increments, returns Home and reopens with shell text and counter retained; no browser errors.

Public API documentation, an illustrative snippet, minor changeset, multi-entry example and production browser coverage are included.

## Publication gate notes

The initial local gate compared against a stale fork main and counted unrelated upstream commits. Local remotes now fetch canonical main while pushing the contribution to tao-io's fork. No upstream history was rewritten and no hook was bypassed.

The complete hook then passed formatting, changesets, lint, dead-code analysis, script typecheck and 190 script tests. Its prebundle check counted the test-only Deferred import despite the distribution compiler excluding test files. The scan now follows the compiler's test exclusion; it verifies the same 38 published runtime namespaces without adding test dependencies to consumer optimization.

The complete framework pre-push hook finished and published commit `0d02ada98` without bypass. Workspace builds, typechecks and test commands completed. Website Chromium returned 13 passed and one flaky existing Combobox navigation test (first attempt timed out waiting for the Documentation Combobox link, retry passed). This is not a clean browser-suite pass; its failure artifact is retained. The contribution's separate production routing check passed with retries disabled. Exact committed-diff review of both commits found no evidence-backed defects; the reviewer executed no checks.

Original labels: `P2`, `size/XL`.
title: feat(foldkit): activate typed lazy compositions inside one runtime
